idea: Notion or Google Sheets sync of the pilot control sheet
why:
Chloe asked for a Notion-style tracker. The current local
CSV+XLSX flow is the first cut; future versions could push
to Notion or a Google Sheet on each merge so Chloe never
needs to clone the repo.

Intake fields live in code today. A self-serve intake builder
would let a studio author its own intake form without a code
change. Out of scope for the controlled pilot.

Surface ops_alerts inside the app (owner-only) so Chloe can
review silent failures (SMS give-ups, manual fee retries,
stripe webhook signature mismatches) without a SQL query.

Build the viewable copy promised by the PR #159 footnote.
Render the template snapshot + signature row as a PDF the
client (or the studio) can save.

Today a new studio is created via SQL by the operator. A
self-serve flow (sign up, create studio, add practitioner,
connect Stripe) would unlock broader pilot.

Once Hone has multiple paying studios, charge a monthly
subscription. Independent of the client-card pipeline. Needs
a separate Stripe account or product model.

idea: Right-to-erasure / export flow for client data
why:
PIPEDA gives clients a right to erasure and a right to access
their data. Today only the practitioner can act on this; a
self-serve client export + erasure flow is the long-term
answer.

practitioners.calendar_feed_token is stored raw today. A DB
compromise would yield usable feed tokens. Migration to
hash + raw-token-only-on-rotate would reduce blast radius.
See docs/03 risk 2.

studios.require_card_on_file = true is the gate. The SQL
backend has been in prod since migration 0032 but the public
booking UI does not surface a card-collection step. Wire it
up when live payments unblock.

Read-only ICS feed exists today. Two-way sync would let Chloe
block time directly from her Google Calendar and have Hone
honor it.
